same_sample.basis: the arrays of the two GAinS studies are each other's most similar sample, and each pair carries the same GAinS patient code in its records; ArrayExpress deposited them without barcodes. The values are those of one array: over the genes that both deposits measure by a single probe, every pair agrees exactly in rank (rank correlation 1.0). The agreement over all genes is lower because the normalized matrix of E-MTAB-4451 holds fewer probes than the raw table of E-MTAB-5274, so for some genes measured by several probes the two deposits keep different probes (gene_matrices.preferred_probe_quality of the annotation stage). The receipt of stage 02 (identity.found_by_entry) records the number of pairs, their range of correlation and their lowest margin.

the study states that the samples of February 2024 were added for consistency with the publication beside those of December 2020; samples of 2020 are each other's most similar sample with a sample of 2024, and each pair carries the same leukocyte count, sex and patient in its record. The receipt of stage 02 (identity.found_by_entry) records the number of pairs, their range of correlation and their lowest margin.

the libraries of the two Osaka studies are each other's most similar sample, and every pair carries the same patient code in its titles (COV13, P7, P19, P25 and others); the counts differ because the studies were quantified separately. GSE228541 holds identical counts of most libraries of GSE243217, which the files link, so a library linked here joins all three studies; because such a copy would stand beside a library as its next most similar sample and hide the pair, the screen compares distinct samples only. The receipt of stage 02 (identity.found_by_entry) records the number of pairs, their range of correlation and their lowest margin.

libraries of the two series, submitted together, are each other's most similar sample with a margin over any other sample that is larger than between any two samples of one patient in the resource; the records name them differently (EG8, EG9 and EG10 in GSE341837, SPTD11, SPTD13 and SPTD14 in GSE341840), so the link rests on the values. The receipt of stage 02 (identity.found_by_entry) records the number of pairs, their range of correlation and their lowest margin.

replicates.basis: the libraries form pairs of consecutive samples (Control 1 and Control 2, Sepsis 1 and Sepsis 2, and so on) that are each other's most similar sample, while no other two samples of the study agree as closely; each pair is taken as two libraries of one sample. The receipt of stage 02 (identity.found_by_entry) records the number of pairs, their range of correlation and their lowest margin.

record_links.basis: GSE131411 marks records as re-analyses in their titles; each title carries the patient and time code of a record of GSE110487 (E07T1, G01T1 and so on), from the same investigators, so each is that library counted again. Every record that the title marks must give its key (the pattern 'required'). The receipt of stage 02 (record_links.pairs) records the number of pairs.

patient_namespaces.name: GSE110487_GSE131411

patient_namespaces.name: EARLI
patient_namespaces.basis: both studies name their patients by the code of the EARLI cohort (EARLI_10456 and so on); their records share 124 codes, and the expression of most shared patients is most similar to their own samples in the other study.
